newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Dairy Board lifts interim milk price.
newsitem.headline: NZ Dairy Board lifts interim milk price.

text.p: The New Zealand Dairy Board said on Thursday it had increased its advance price for milk to NZ$3.05 cents/milksolids from $2.90.
The board said that since the advance price was last reviewed in October, international market conditions had remained relatively stable.
However, commodity price levels for butter were down by about US$600 a tonne, or 30 percent, while milkpowder and casein prices were about 10 percent below levels ruling 12 months ago.
"The season has seen record production, with the milkflow running 10 percent ahead of the 1994/95 season and well ahead of the optimal growth target of three to four percent," the board said.
"This high level of production has required an aggressive sales programme throughout the year to ensure stocks are at reasonable balance at the end of the year. This objective has been achieved."
While the board's added value strategies were contributing strongly to returns, that contribution was being more than offset by the appreciation of the New Zealand dollar.
"We expect the impact of the dollar's apppreciation on payout to be 18 cents/kg milksolids over the whole year," the board said.
"For the balance of the year any further impact will be minimal as a consequence of forward cover contracts already in place.
"Taking all these factors into account, the board remains confident that the final payout for the season will remain within the $3.15-$3.20 range."
